title: SDM-1 — Studio Documentation Rationalisation
summary: review and apply an approved current-state rationalisation of Studio-owned documentation without inferring ownership or retiring history automatically
content_html:
SDM-1 — Studio Documentation Rationalisation

Complete Result

The Studio documentation has one reviewed current-state baseline: retained documents have clear durable purposes and correct parents, the Studio entry page routes to the useful current owners, redundant or stale manual material has an explicit approved disposition, and affected links remain exact.

This is a documentation delivery. It changes no Studio or Docs Viewer production behavior.

Why Now

Full-text search will make the complete Studio corpus more visible. Improving retrieval before reviewing the corpus would rank duplicated, stale, or poorly owned material more effectively without making that material more trustworthy.

The current Studio subtree contains 39 documents. Thirty-one are direct Studio children, only 15 of those are linked from the Studio entry page, and several cross-application documents elsewhere contain substantial Studio authority. Those counts identify review pressure; they do not determine the outcome.

Scope

Review:

  • Studio, its 38 descendants, and every current entry-page link
  • plausible Studio-owned durable documents parented elsewhere
  • short, low-inbound, overlapping, verification-only, or manually duplicated documents revealed by the inventory
  • inbound and outbound document links affected by any proposed reparent, consolidation, Notes transfer, or retirement
  • the boundary between durable current state, active Roadmap planning, and completed history

Classify each reviewed document as one of:

  • retain unchanged
  • update in place
  • reparent with the same doc_id
  • consolidate into a named durable owner
  • propose transfer to external Notes
  • propose retirement

Classification is a proposal until the review gate is accepted. Reparenting is not inferred from code-path frequency, and consolidation, Notes transfer, and retirement are never applied without exact approval.

Current Authority To Inspect

  • Studio source documents under docs-viewer/scopes/studio/source/documents/
  • parent_id and the generated Studio index tree for navigation ownership
  • Studio Overview and Studio for the current entry model
  • current code, configuration, and focused tests only where a document's claimed authority needs verification
  • ordinary rendered document links for exact inbound-link impact

No production or test file is part of the expected rationalisation diff.

SDM-1.0 — Inventory And Decision Gate

Produce a concise review table containing:

  • exact doc_id, title, current parent, and durable purpose
  • inbound-link and entry-page visibility signals
  • proposed classification and destination where applicable
  • exact source documents and links that an accepted change would touch
  • explicit production and test files, expected to remain none

Pay particular attention to:

  • duplicated current-state explanations split across short documents
  • verification records presented as durable architecture
  • manually copied registry, route, endpoint, or report inventories
  • documents whose parent implies the wrong owner
  • completed feature history that no longer helps current Roadmap navigation
  • useful low-level reference material that should remain searchable even when it is not linked from the Studio entry page

Review stop: present the complete proposed table, expected source-document set, and rough documentation diff before editing any pre-existing document in the SDM-1 application set, changing a parent, moving material to Notes, consolidating content, or retiring a document.

SDM-1.0 Review Result — 2026-08-13

The review covered all 38 pre-existing descendants of Studio, their exact ordinary document links, the Studio entry page, and the cross-application documents with the strongest Studio ownership signals. Current implementation was checked where a document claimed an active route, service, command, or projection.

The current tree has 31 direct Studio children. The proposed shape has 15: user-facing Studio workflows stay easy to reach, while focused source, projection, route, API, config, and build documents sit beneath their durable owners. No retained document changes doc_id or filename.

No source filename changes, new durable documents, Notes writes, production files, or test files are proposed. The eight retiring documents contain 328 source lines. The retained owners should need roughly 100–140 added or rewritten lines plus eight parent-field changes, for an expected net reduction of about 180–220 source lines across 25 affected source files.

Generated follow-through is expected to update the affected by-ID payloads, remove eight retired by-ID payloads and search entries, and rewrite the Studio tree, Recent, and search indexes. The direct Studio child count should fall from 31 to 15 while the total Studio scope falls by eight documents.

Existing Link Baseline

A read-only exact-target scan checked 680 ordinary same-scope Markdown links and found 17 unresolved targets already present in the wider Studio scope. Two occur only in the retired Project State stubs proposed for removal. The other 15 are outside the exact 25-file application above and mostly connect retained feature or delivery history to documents no longer present in the repository-backed Studio scope; absence is not treated as proof that the historical material was deleted rather than moved to external Notes.

SDM-1 does not silently absorb that separate Roadmap/history reconciliation. The application must introduce no new unresolved target, must remove the two issues owned by its retiring stubs, and must validate every changed ordinary link directly. A whole-scope zero-broken-links claim remains outside this delivery unless the remaining 15-target reconciliation is separately approved.

Gate Decision Needed

Approve, revise, or reject this exact application shape. Approval authorizes only the 25-file documentation rationalisation and its generated follow-through. It does not authorize SDM-2, Search Mechanics implementation, external Notes mutation, or additional cleanup discovered during application.

Approved Application

After explicit acceptance of SDM-1.0:

  1. apply only the approved document, parent, and link changes;
  2. preserve every retained exact doc_id;
  3. rebuild the Studio docs and search projections;
  4. verify the generated tree and affected inbound links;
  5. run the focused broken-links audit and git diff --check; and
  6. present the resulting source/generated delta for closeout review.

Do not begin SDM-2 or Search Mechanics implementation during this delivery.

SDM-1.1 — Applied Result And Closeout Gate

The approved application was applied on 2026-08-13 without widening its production, test, Notes, or document-identity boundary.

  • all 17 retained application documents were updated in place and kept their exact doc_id and filename;
  • all eight approved consolidation or retired-stub documents were removed after their durable content and live inbound links moved;
  • the application source delta is 122 insertions and 376 deletions across the exact 25 files, a net reduction of 254 lines;
  • the Studio direct-child count fell from 31 to 15 and the complete Studio scope fell from 245 to 237 documents;
  • Catalogue source and payload references now sit below Catalogue Architecture, the field registry sits below Studio Domain Config, route/config references sit below Studio Runtime, Local Studio APIs sits below Local Studio App, and Configuration Map sits below Dev Home;
  • generated follow-through modified the 17 retained by-ID payloads, removed the eight retired by-ID payloads and search entries, and refreshed the tree, Recent, and search indexes.

Focused validation:

  • build_docs.py --scope studio --write: 237 documents, 13 tree roots, 10 Recent entries, zero warnings;
  • build_search.py --scope studio --write: current Studio search projection, no additional write required;
  • generated tree: 15 exact Studio children with the accepted nested owners;
  • generated JSON: all document, tree, Recent, and search payloads parse successfully;
  • broken-links audit: 15 pre-existing unresolved targets remain, down from 17; none originate in a changed retained document and no retired ID remains a live link target;
  • git diff --check: clean.

Review stop: approve closeout or request a correction to SDM-1. Approval may mark this delivery done and move Studio Documentation Maintenance to SDM-2. It does not authorize SDM-2 implementation in the same closeout action.

Completion Evidence

  • the accepted classification table maps exactly to the applied source diff
  • the Studio entry and generated tree expose the accepted current owners
  • every changed link retains an exact scope and doc_id
  • no unapproved document is moved, consolidated, transferred, or retired
  • focused Docs Viewer builds and link validation pass
  • durable Studio documentation reflects the accepted baseline

Durable Destination

Studio and the retained domain documents own the resulting current-state map. This delivery retains only its approved decision table and completion evidence until closeout disposition is explicitly reviewed.
